topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations for learning the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational concepts, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general architecture of complement, its naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of component C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct biochemical pathways that initiate complement activation and drive it toward the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms executed by activated complement, including opsonization, inflammation, and direct pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use specific regulatory proteins to prevent unintended complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease presentations and clinical consequences associated with deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, have evolved specialized mechanisms to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing for the session and previews the upcoming lecture on adaptive immunity.
